title: A Hymn for the Portrait
premise: Juniper Fairweather, a property surveyor who has spent his life keeping his head down and his doors counted, is sent to appraise Hollowmere House before its demolition. When an excavation crew unearths a door sealed from the inside—bricked shut in 1974—the house begins appraising him back: measuring his worth, cataloguing his habits, deciding whether he is inventory or heir. Juniper discovers the house was built to hold something the previous owners stole from it, and that it has been waiting fifty years for someone to return what was taken. To save the found family of misfits who gather around him at Hollowmere, Juniper must give back the one thing he cannot bear to lose—his own name—and learn that identity freely surrendered is not erased but finally claimed.
about_author: Hazel Kavanagh is the pen name of a former building inspector who spent eleven years walking through other people's empty houses and never quite shaking the feeling that some of them were walking through her. She writes horror about architecture, obligation, and the terrible intimacy of being noticed.

chapters.title: The Inventory
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. He arrives at Hollowmere House for a routine pre-demolition appraisal, methodically counting doors (eleven) and checking lights that flicker in rooms with no wiring. The house feels attentive. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as professionalism; Juniper's relief at being somewhere no one knows him.

chapters.title: Eleven Doors, Twelve Frames
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. He finds twelve doorframes but only eleven doors—one frame bricked over from the inside, mortar dated 1974. That night, the house rearranges its measurements; every room is exactly one inch smaller than his notes say. Emotional beat: creeping dread as his careful systems fail for the first time.

chapters.title: What the Crew Unearthed
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, shifting to crew foreman Dara Okafor's POV mid-chapter. The excavation opens the sealed door; inside is a small room containing a child's belongings and a ledger listing names—including, impossibly, 'J. Fairweather.' Emotional beat: vertigo of recognition; the past reaching forward.

chapters.title: The Neighbors Who Stayed
chapters.summary: Dara's POV. Locals warn them off: retired teacher Mabel Crane and handyman Silas Voss, who both lived near Hollowmere in 1974 and have quietly kept vigil ever since. They reveal the house 'chose' keepers once. Emotional beat: warmth of found family forming around shared fear.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Names
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The ledger records transactions: things taken from the house in 1974—a mirror, a christening gown, a name—and the debt accruing interest ever since. Juniper realizes his own entry was written decades before his birth. Emotional beat: identity shaken; duty inherited without consent.

chapters.title: Appraised
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The house begins evaluating him directly—doors open only when he proves useful, lights reward honesty, a locked room punishes a lie. He starts to feel seen in a way that is both violating and, shamefully, welcome. Emotional beat: love against self-protection; the terror of mattering.

Mabel's POV, a flashback chapter. The original owners' daughter vanished behind the sealed door after her parents stripped the house of its 'heart' to sell it. Mabel helped brick the door—from the outside, she always believed. Emotional beat: guilt across generations; the cost of looking away.

chapters.title: Interest Due
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Demolition is moved up; the house panics, walls sweating, doors multiplying. It takes Silas briefly into itself, releasing him aged and silent. The ledger updates: payment required within three days. Emotional beat: rising stakes; found family now hostage to the debt.

chapters.title: The Return
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, climax. In the sealed room, Juniper understands the stolen item was the house's name, which became his family's surname. He speaks it aloud, surrendering 'Fairweather,' offering himself as keeper rather than victim. The house must choose between consuming him and accepting him. Emotional beat: sacrifice transformed into belonging.

chapters.title: A Hymn for the Portrait
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, resolution. The demolition is cancelled; Hollowmere stands, renamed. Juniper keeps the lights on by choice now, doors counted not from fear but care, with Mabel, Dara, and recovering Silas as household. His portrait joins the others on the stairwell wall. Emotional beat: quiet peace; invisibility traded for home.
